claims.claim: On 9 July 2002 it was announced that the WHI estrogen-plus-progestin trial had been halted early.
claims.episode_span: on 9 July, the data safety monitoring board halted the largest part of the Women’s Health Initiative trial three years early
claims.source_title: ACOG Statement of WHI Report | Sexual Medicine | BUMC
claims.supporting_quote: On July 9, 2002, it was announced that the Women's Health Initiative (WHI) study evaluating combined estrogen and progestin use in postmenopausal women was halted.

claims.claim: The WHI estrogen-plus-progestin trial enrolled 16,608 women aged 50-79 with an intact uterus.
claims.episode_span: The Women’s Health Initiative enrolled 16,608 women aged 50–79 with an intact uterus
claims.source_title: Hormone Therapy Study Stopped Due To Increased Breast Cancer Risk, Lack Of Overall Benefit | ScienceDaily (NHLBI release)
claims.supporting_quote: The estrogen plus progestin trial of the WHI involved 16,608 women ages 50 to 79 years with an intact uterus.

claims.claim: The WHI hazard ratios were 1.29 for coronary heart disease, 1.41 for stroke, 2.13 for pulmonary embolism, and 1.26 for invasive breast cancer.
claims.episode_span: the hazard ratio for coronary heart disease was 1.29, for stroke 1.41, for pulmonary embolism 2.13, and for invasive breast cancer 1.26
claims.source_title: ACOG Statement of WHI Report | Sexual Medicine | BUMC
claims.supporting_quote: Breast cancer risk 1.26 [95% confidence interval (CI) 1.00-1.59] o Coronary heart disease risk 1.29 [CI 1.02-1.63] o Stroke risk 1.41 [CI 1.07-1.85] o Pulmonary embolism risk 2.13 [CI 1.39-3.25]

claims.claim: Per 10,000 women per year, the trial found 7 more CHD events, 8 more strokes, 8 more pulmonary embolisms, 8 more invasive breast cancers, 6 fewer colorectal cancers, and 5 fewer hip fractures.
claims.episode_span: seven additional coronary events, eight additional strokes, and eight additional breast cancers per 10,000 women per year, against six fewer colorectal cancers and five fewer hip fractures
claims.source_title: What did the 2002 Women's Health Initiative study actually say about postmenopausal HRT? | Natural Womanhood
claims.supporting_quote: Over 1 year, 10 000 women taking estrogen plus progestin compared with placebo might experience 7 more CHD events, 8 more strokes, 8 more PEs, 8 more invasive breast cancers, 6 fewer colorectal cancers, and 5 fewer hip fractures.

claims.claim: The trial, scheduled to run until 2005, was stopped after an average follow-up of 5.2 years.
claims.episode_span: After 5.2 years the hazard ratio for coronary heart disease was 1.29
claims.source_title: Hormone Therapy Study Stopped Due To Increased Breast Cancer Risk, Lack Of Overall Benefit | ScienceDaily (NHLBI release)
claims.supporting_quote: The study, which was scheduled to run until 2005, was stopped after an average follow-up of 5.2 years.

claims.claim: In 1986 the FDA announced in the Federal Register that Premarin (0.625 mg daily) was effective for prevention of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women.
claims.episode_span: The Food and Drug Administration recognized estrogens for osteoporosis prevention in 1986
claims.supporting_quote: In 1986, FDA announced in the Federal Register that a 0.625 mg dose of Premarin daily was found to be effective for prevention of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women

claims.claim: Feminine Forever, a 1966 book by American gynecologist Robert A. Wilson, framed menopause as a disease state and strongly advocated estrogen therapy.
claims.episode_span: In 1966, Brooklyn gynecologist Robert A. Wilson published *Feminine Forever*, arguing that estrogen deficiency was a treatable disease state
claims.supporting_quote: Feminine Forever is a 1966 book written by American gynecologist Robert A. Wilson . [ 1 ] [ 2 ] The book characterized menopause and associated symptoms as a serious disease state and strongly advocated the use of estrogen -based menopausal hormone therapy
